The network emerged from a workshop in Helsinki in August 2015. Coordinated by Uppsala University’s Linde Lindkvist, University of Helsinki’s Johan Strang and University of Oslo’s Hanne Hagtvedt Vik, the network organizes panels and workshops on various aspects of the import of human rights norms in Nordic local and national contexts, as well as the significance of Nordic actors in international human rights diplomacy.

Vik was the initiator and director, together with Professor Hilde Henriksen Waage, of the Oslo Contemporary International History Network, which gathered internationally leading professors and early-career researchers to assess and further develop new trends in the field (2010-2012). She led the establishment of the Norwegian Research School in History which is a cooperation between nine Norwegian universities and university colleges (2018-2022).

Vik has taught international history in interdisciplinary and history courses at bachelor's and master's level. She has also taught US history and Norwegian foreign policy history. Vik has supervised students at all levels. During the spring term of 2011, she was a guest lecturer in human rights history at Yale University.
